chunks: And Ali ibn Habashi ibn Qauni narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, who said:

I used to see at my uncle Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal's place an old man from Baghdad who used to joke with my uncle. One day he said to him: 'There is no worse group in the world than you, O people of the Shia' - or he said 'the Rafidah'. My uncle asked him: 'Why? May Allah curse you.' He replied: 'I am the son-in-law of Ahmad ibn Abi Bashir al-Sarraj. When death approached him, he said to me: 'I have ten thousand dinars in deposit for Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). After his death, I did not hand them over to his son and claimed that he was not dead! By Allah, save me from the Fire and hand them over to al-Rida.' By Allah, we did not return even one dirham from that and left him to burn with it in the Fire of Hell.'

key_terms.الرَّفَضَة: The Rafidah (a term for Shia, often used by opponents)
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (Imam Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ: Musa ibn Ja'far (Imam Musa al-Kadim, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the old man from Baghdad regarding the ten thousand dinars and Imam Musa al-Kadim?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the theological error of the Waqifiyya, who halted their belief in the Imamate at Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.), by linking their doctrinal stagnation to spiritual punishment. The story of the Baghdad merchant, who withheld the Imam’s deposit while claiming he was not dead, serves as a metaphor for how attachment to the Imam’s person without recognizing his successor leads to being 'burned' in Hellfire alongside the withheld wealth. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that Waqifism is not merely a historical sect but a condition of the heart that results in divine retribution for failing to acknowledge the continuity of the Imamate.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 69 - Ali bin Habashi bin Qauni has narrated from Husain bin Ahmad bin Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal that he said:

I was with my uncle, Ali bin Hasan bin Faddal, when I saw an old man from Baghdad joking with my uncle. One day that old man said: In the whole world, no group of Shia is worse than you. My Uncle asked: Why, may Allah curse you? He replied: I was the son-in-law of Ahmad bin Shubbar Siraj. In his last moments, he said: I have ten thousand dinars in my possession, which originally belonged to Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s), but when he passed away, I refused to hand them over to Imam Ali Ridha (a.s) and claimed that he was not dead. I put you under oath to save me from Hell fire and hand over the money to Imam Ridha (a.s). But by Allah, we did not return even one dirham from that and left him to burn in the Fire of Hell.
